questions.question: What is the difference between the compound interest compounded annually and the simple interest on Rs.16,000 for 3 years at 5% per annum?
questions.solution:
**Formula:**

Let P = Principal, R = rate of interest and N = time period

Simple interest = PNR/100

Compound interest = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ - P

**Calculation:**

Simple interest = 16000 × 3 × 5/100 = Rs.2400

Compound interest = 16000(1 + 5/100)³ - 16000 = Rs.2522

**∴ Required difference = 2522 - 2400 = Rs.122**

questions.question: A spherical solid lead ball of radius 9 cm is melted and small solid lead balls of radius 3 mm are made. What is the number of small balls made?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Radius of small spherical balls = 3mm

Radius of large ball = 9cm = 90mm

**Formula:**

Volume of sphere = 4/3 × π × r³

**Calculation:**

Volume of large ball = 4/3 × π × 90³

Volume of small ball = 4/3 × π × 3³

Let number of small ball prepared from large ball be N.

⇒ 4/3 × π × 90³ = N × 4/3 × π × 3³

⇒ N = 27000

**∴ there are 27000 small balls prepared.**

questions.question: Rs.6,060 is divided between A, B and C in such a way that if it reduces Rs.15 from A's share, Rs.20 from B's share, and Rs.25 from C's share, then The ratio of their parts becomes 5 ∶ 7 ∶ 8. How much was C's original share (in Rs.)?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Total money = Rs.6060

**Calculation:**

Let The amount of money A, B, and C have after reduction be Rs.5a, Rs.7a, and Rs.8a respectively.

⇒ (5a + 15) + (7a + 20) + (8a + 25) = 6060

⇒ a = 300

New share of C = Rs.2400

**∴ Original share of C = 2400 + 25 = Rs.2425**

questions.question: A publisher sells a book to a wholesale dealer at a profit of 30%. The wholesaler sells the book to a retailer at a profit of 25%. The book is then sold to a customer for Rs.312, by earning a profit of 20%. What is the cost price (in Rs.) of the book for the wholesale dealer?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Profit of publisher = 30%

Profit of wholesaler = 25%

Profit of retailer = 20%

**Concept Used:**

Selling price = Cost price × (100 + profit %)/100

**Calculation:**

Selling Price of book for customer = Rs.312

Cost price of book for seller who sells to customer = 312 × 100/120 = Rs.260

Selling price of a book for wholesale = Rs.260

**∴ Cost price of book for seller = 260 × 100/125 = Rs.208**

questions.question: A loan is returned in two equal yearly instalments of Rs.5,808. What is the total amount of the loan if the rate of compound interest, compounded annually, is 10% per annum?
questions.solution:
**Formula:**

Let P = Principal and A = equal instalment

P = A/(1 + R/100)¹ + A/(1 + R/100)² + .....+ A/(1 + R/100)ⁿ

**Calculation:**

Amount to be paid of loan = 5808/(1 + 10/100)¹ + 5808/(1 + 10/100)²

⇒ 5280 + 4800

⇒ 10080

**∴ Amount to be paid as loan Rs.10080**

questions.question: The average score of a group of students in a test is 64. If 20% students obtained an average score of 91 and 25% students obtained an average score of 31, then what is the average score (correct to one decimal place) of the remaining students?
questions.solution:
**Concept Used:**

Sum = Average × Number of observation

**Calculation:**

Let the total number of students in a group be N.

Total score of group = 64N

Total score of 20% students = 20N/100 × 91

Total score of 25% students = 25N/100 × 31

Total score of 55% students = 64N - (20N/100 × 91 + 25N/100 × 31) = 38.05N

**∴ Required average = 38.05N/(55N/100) = 69.2**

questions.question: Equal square tiles are to be fixed on a wall, 3 m 50 cm in length and 4 m in height. How many largest possible tiles are needed to cover the wall?
questions.solution:

questions.question: A person covered a certain distance at some speed. Had he moved 6 km/h faster, he would have taken 30 minutes less. If he had moved 4 km/h slower, he would have taken 30 minutes more. What is his original speed (in km/h)?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

If the man moved 6 km/h faster, he would have taken 30 minutes less. If he had moved 4 km/h slower, he would have taken 30 minutes more.

**Concept Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

**Calculation:**

Let the original speed be m km/h and the distance is x km

For the first case get,

x/m - x/(m + 6) = 30/60 [30 mins = 30/60 hours]

⇒ x(m + 6 - m)/m(m + 6) = 1/2

⇒ 6x/m(m + 6) = 1/2

⇒ x = m(m + 6)/12 ----(1)

Again from the 2nd case get,

x/(m - 4) - x/m = 30/60 [30 mins = 30/60 hours]

⇒ x(m - m + 4)/m(m - 4) = 1/2

⇒ x = m(m - 4)/8 ----(2)

From (1) and (2) get,

m(m + 6)/12 = m(m - 4)/8

⇒ 2(m² + 6m) = 3(m² - 4m)

⇒ 2m² + 12m = 3m² - 12m

⇒ m² - 24m = 0

⇒ m(m - 24) = 0

⇒ m = 0 or m = 24

m can't be 0 so, m = 24

**∴ original speed is 24kmph.**

questions.question: Henry is working in a company. From his monthly salary, 25% is deducted as house rent, 15% is spent on children's education and 18% is spent on other heads. If his monthly savings are Rs.7,560, then what is his monthly salary (in Rs.)?
questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

Let monthly salary of Henry be Rs.m.

⇒ 7560 = m - m × (25/100 + 15/100 + 18/100)

⇒ 7560 = 42m/100

⇒ m = 18000

**∴ Monthly salary of Henry is Rs.18000**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__ 

 **Let the total salary = 100%

100% - (25% + 15% + 18%) = 7560

100 % - 58% = 7560.

42% = 7560

1% = 7560/42 = 180

**∴ 100% = 18000**

questions.question: A and B together can finish a work in 10 days, B and C together can finish the same work in 15 days, and A and C together can finish the same work in 20 days. In how many days can c alone finish the same work?
questions.solution:
**Concept Used:**

If a person can do a task in x days then in 1 day work will be completed 1/x part

**Calculation:**

1/A + 1/B = 1/10

1/B + 1/C = 1/15

1/A + 1/C = 1/20

Then,

⇒ 1/A - 1/C = 1/30

Solving,

⇒ 1/C = 1/120

**∴ In 120 days, C alone can finish the work.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__** Calculation:

A & B together complete the task = 10 days.

B & C together complete the task = 15 days.

A & C together complete the task = 20 days.

Total work = LCM of (10, 15 & 20) = 60 units.

The combined efficiency of A & B = 60/10 = 6 units

The combined efficiency of B & C = 60/15 = 4 units

The combined efficiency of A & C = 60/ 20 = 3 units

Total efficiency = 2(A + B +C) = 13 (6 + 4 + 3)

⇒ Total efficiency (A + B + C) = 13/2 = 6.5 units

Each efficiency of A = (6.5 - 4) = 2.5 units

Efficiency of B = (6.5 - 3) = 3.5 units.

Efficiency of C = (6.5 - 6) = 0.5 units.

Time taken by C alone to complete the task = 60/(0.5) = 120 days.

**∴ C alone finish the same work in 120 days.**

questions.question: A shopkeeper marks his goods at 32% above the cost price. He sells three-fifth of the goods at the marked price, one-fifth at a discount of 20% on the market price, and the remaining at 40% discount on the marked price. What is his profit/loss percentage?
questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

Let cost price of goods be Rs.100

Marked price of goods = 100 × 132/100 = Rs.132

Selling price when discount is 20% = 132 × 80/100 = Rs.105.6

Selling price when discount is 40% = 132 × 60/100 = Rs.79.2

Total selling price of goods = 3/5 × 132 + 1/5 × 105.6 + 1/5 × 79.2 = Rs.116.16

**∴ Profit percentage = (116.16 - 100)/100 × 100 = 16.16%**

questions.question: What is the number that is always a factor of the sum of a 2-digit number and a number obtained by interchanging the digits of the number?
questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

Let two digit number be 10a + b and number after interchanging digits be 10b + a.

⇒ 10a + b + 10b + a = 11a + 11b = 11(a + b)

**∴ From above, 11 is always a factor of their sum.**

questions.question: The value of a machine depreciates at the rate of 25% each year. If the difference between its value at the end of the second year and the third year is Rs.24,000, then what is the value (in Rs.) of the machine at the end of the first year?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The value of a machine depreciates at the rate of 25% each year.

**Concept Used:**

Price after depreciation = Original price × (100 - depreciation %)/100

**Calculation:**

Let the value of the machine at the end of first year be Rs.a

The value of the machine at the end of second year = a × 75/100

The value of the machine at the end of third year = a × 75/100 × 75/100

Accordingly,

a × 75/100 - a × 75/100 × 75/100 = 24000

⇒ a = 128000

**∴ The value of the machine at the end of the first year is Rs.128000.**
